# Pi integration

## What gets installed

```
~/.pi/agent/extensions/local-photo/index.ts
```

Two lines, generated by the installer:

```ts
// Generated by local-photo-ai-m5 scripts/install.sh — do not edit.
export { default } from "/abs/path/to/local-photo-ai-m5/dist/pi/index.js";
```

The implementation stays in the repository (`src/pi/index.ts`) so it is
version-controlled, typechecked and built alongside everything else. Only the
pointer lives in Pi's directory.

Pi discovers `~/.pi/agent/extensions/*/index.ts` automatically, so the tools are
available **in every repository** with no per-project setup. `/reload` picks up
changes without restarting Pi.

## Why an extension and not MCP

Pi has no built-in MCP client — its own documentation says so explicitly:

> It intentionally does not include built-in MCP, sub-agents, permission
> popups, plan mode, to-dos, or background bash.

So the Pi integration is native. It is **not** a bridge to this project's MCP
server: it imports `LocalPhotoService` directly and calls the same core the CLI
and the MCP server call. One implementation, three doorways — see
[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Tools

| tool | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `image_generate` | make a photograph, return absolute paths |
| `image_upscale` | enlarge an existing image conservatively |
| `image_health` | is local generation ready on this machine |
| `image_prompt_preview` | show the brief without spending a generation |

`image_*` rather than `photo_*` because models reach for `image_generate`
first. If you want the aliases as well:

```bash
LOCAL_PHOTO_TOOL_ALIASES=1 pi
```

which additionally registers `photo_generate`, `photo_upscale` and
`photo_health`. Off by default so the tool list stays small — every registered
tool costs context on every turn.

### `image_generate`

| parameter | notes |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt` | plain language, Portuguese or English. **Required.** |
| `preset` | `natural` (default) · `professional` · `lifestyle` · `clinical` · `product` · `smartphone` |
| `size` | `square` · `portrait` · `landscape` · `wide` · `hero` · `post` · `post-portrait` · `story` |
| `width` / `height` | explicit pixels, overrides `size` |
| `count` | 1–4. Default 1. |
| `seed` | for reproducibility |
| `output` | the **final** file: `./public/assets/hero.jpg`, or a trailing `/` for a directory |
| `upscale` | `final` (default: Lanczos 1.5×) · `off` · `auto` |
| `preview` | also return the image inline so the agent can look at it |

The unscaled render is kept beside the final one as `hero.raw.jpg` and is
reported back with it. It never overwrites the path the agent asked for.

`preview: true` is genuinely useful — it lets the agent check whether the photo
actually matches the page before wiring it into the HTML — but it costs image
tokens on every turn it stays in context, so it is opt-in.

## The workflow this exists for

```bash
cd ~/src/cluemed
pi
```

> Crie uma foto realista de uma médica atendendo uma idosa que combine com essa
> landing page e coloque no hero.

What Pi does, with no further prompting:

1. reads the repo — the HTML, the CSS, the palette, the tone
2. infers the visual identity
3. writes a plain-language intent
4. calls `image_generate` with a preset and an output path under `public/`
5. gets an absolute path back
6. edits the HTML to use it

Qwen never sees a checkpoint filename, a sampler, a LoRA weight or a Metal
flag. It sees a scene description and a file path. That is the entire point.

## Prompting the agent well

The tool description already tells the model not to pad prompts with quality
words, but if you want to steer it further, the useful instructions are about
*content*, not *rendering*:

| say this | not this |
| --- | --- |
| "brazilian clinic, two people, mid-conversation" | "ultra realistic 8k masterpiece" |
| "nobody looking at the camera" | "cinematic lighting, award winning" |
| "the laptop should look used" | "hyper detailed, sharp focus" |

Everything in the right-hand column actively makes results worse. The engine
never emits those terms itself, and there is a test that keeps it that way.

## Troubleshooting

**Tools do not appear.**

```bash
ls ~/.pi/agent/extensions/local-photo/index.ts   # exists?
pi list                                          # extensions Pi knows about
```

Inside Pi, `/reload` re-reads auto-discovered extensions.

**`Cannot find module`.** The shim points at `dist/`, so the project must be
built and must not have moved:

```bash
cd /path/to/local-photo-ai-m5 && npm run build
./scripts/install.sh          # rewrites the shim with the current path
```

**A tool errors with "model not installed".** Ask `image_health`, or run
`local-photo doctor` in a terminal.

**The generation is slow the first time.** It is: the model loads per call.
That is the on-demand design — nothing is resident between generations. See
[BENCHMARK.md](BENCHMARK.md) for what that actually costs here.
